summary: 502/503 surge at edge during short-lived streaming bursts causing elevated error rate for dedicated customer
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 11:10-11:45 UTC KiteBank reported a spike of 502/503 responses from the Redwood API for short-lived streaming sessions. Impact: ~12% of requests (per their telemetry) returned 5xx; request volume for the customer returned to normal but error rate persisted during short streaming bursts. Customer impact: user-facing failures in KiteBank's chat flows during a scheduled load test; revenue-impacting for production flows.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 11:08 UTC: KiteBank begins automated short-lived streaming burst (hundreds of concurrent connections, each streaming ~3-10s then close).
- 2026-03-10 11:12 UTC: Alerts triggered for elevated 5xx rate from apigw routing to us-east.
- 2026-03-10 11:25 UTC: Support ingested customer logs and asked for correlation IDs; SRE observed proxy connection churn and runtime proxy logs showing TLS session errors.
- 2026-03-10 11:40 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied (connection_limit increase and short keepalive tuning). Client-side retry backoff recommended.
- 2026-03-12 10:00 UTC: Root cause patch rolled to edge-proxy and kernel tuning applied to dedicated pool; monitored for 72 hours.
steps_to_reproduce: From a client in us-east, open 400 concurrent streaming connections to Redwood hosted endpoint with keepalive disabled and stream short payloads (<10s).
Close connections immediately after receiving the first chunk to simulate many short-lived sessions.
Observe api-gateway metrics and edge-proxy logs; look for elevated 502/503 and `TLS_error: short read` / `connection reset by peer` entries.
Run a second iteration with keepalive enabled and long-lived streams; error rate should drop significantly.
This reproducer is time-sensitive and requires simulating the customer's burst pattern rather than sustained throughput.
logs: apigw: 2026-03-10T11:14:21Z ERROR upstream 172.18.9.45:502 "502 Bad Gateway" path=/v1/generate cid=kb-1a2b3c
edge-proxy: 2026-03-10T11:14:21Z WARN conn=9876 TLS_error: 'short read' while reading from client
serving-runtime: 2026-03-10T11:14:22Z INFO session_close reason=client_disconnect pod=runtime-7bd9 oom=false
kernel: 2026-03-10T11:14:22Z NOTICE fd_count=65432 fd_limit=65536 approaching limits for proxy worker 3
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: serving-runtime OOM or model crash. Evidence: runtime pods did not show OOM; core dumps absent.
Telemetry showed large number of ephemeral TCP connections with very short lifetimes -> connection churn at edge-proxy.
Edge-proxy worker fd and epoll backlog approached kernel limits during bursts (fd_count ~65k, limit 65,536).
TLS short read and conn reset pattern pointed to connection tracking exhaustion rather than application-level failures.
Dedicated pool config had conservative proxy file-descriptor limits and the customer's client test had keepalive disabled, amplifying connection churn.
Increasing proxy ulimit and enabling TCP TIME_WAIT reuse and short keepalive on the host mitigated reproducer in canary environment.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported 12% 5xx during their internal load test. Asked for correlation IDs, sample cURL and approx concurrency. (2026-03-10 11:20)
SRE (Ethan): Noted fd_count approaching limit; asked for kernel tunables and pod limits. Started temporary increase of proxy ulimit on dedicated pool. (2026-03-10 11:32)
Customer (KiteBank-Eng): Provided test harness and observed error rate drop after connection limit bump. Confirmed need for long-term fix. (2026-03-10 12:05)
Eng (Maya Singh): Rolled connection reuse + keepalive guidance to customer and prepared PR to increase default proxy ulimit and add detection for sudden connection-churn events. (2026-03-11 09:40)
SRE (Ethan): Deployed kernel tuning + updated canary images; monitoring shows error rate returned to baseline. Marking incident resolved and scheduling follow-up. (2026-03-12 10:05)
resolution: Root cause: connection churn from many short-lived streaming sessions exhausted edge-proxy file descriptors/epoll capacity resulting in upstream 502/503. Fixes applied: 1) Increased proxy ulimit and epoll backlogs on dedicated pool hosts; 2) Kernel TCP tuning (tcp_tw_reuse, TIME_WAIT parameters) and host keepalive defaults tightened; 3) Added a guard in edge-proxy to surface connection-churn alarms and temporarily reject new ephemeral streams with 429 to avoid cascading 5xx; 4) Customer recommended to enable HTTP keepalive for streaming clients and add jittered backoff on retries. Patch PR https://github.com/redwood/release/pull/7214; runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/edge-conn-limits. Follow-ups: add automatic scaling of proxy workers for dedicated pools (action item assigned INT-4123) and include connection-churn load tests in preflight test suite. Customer validated fix in production and observed error rate returned to <0.5% for the same test pattern.
